text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is diagnosed when your blood pressure readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.
Doctors use the guidelines from the American Heart Association to classify blood pressure levels:

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 / under 80 mm Hg
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 or higher / 90 or higher mm Hg
Hypertensive Crisis (Emergency): Higher than 180 and/or higher than 120 mm Hg
Systolic (top number): Measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): Measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart rests between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: A reading above 180/120 mm Hg requires waiting a few minutes and retesting. If it remains this high and you have warning signs like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, or vision changes, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact your doctor right away.
